stories.title: TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8
stories.reason: CVSS 9.8 remote unauthenticated Linux TCP use-after-free; Anthropic reports Claude wrote a working remote-root exploit after prompting, landmark AI-exploit-dev story with primary source and technical detail.
key_facts: Use-after-free in Linux IPv4 TCP handshake option handling; race lets a freed request-socket options struct be read by another CPU.
Upstream fix (Dumazet, commit e3f33b0) swaps two kfree() for kfree_rcu().
Anthropic's unpublished PoC gets root command execution on MPTCP listener hosts in ~48 min to leak a kernel pointer plus ~5 more min to RCE; reported via Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge.
Go opens MPTCP listeners by default since Go 1.24, widening exposure.
Fixed upstream Oct 11-18, 2026; distro coverage uneven (Debian/SUSE/Oracle UEK/Amazon Linux fixed; Ubuntu/RHEL not yet; AlmaLinux in testing); not in CISA KEV as of report.
36 GitHub repos referenced the CVE by Oct 31, at least 6 claiming a PoC (unverified by author).

stories.title: Malware uses LLMs to rank victims by how much they're worth
stories.reason: Cisco Talos documents real infostealer malware (VOLTA-AUTODOXER) that sends a built dossier of stolen victim data to an LLM (via OpenRouter) which scores victims' monetizable value and OPSEC, with a model fallback chain to dodge refusals - concrete AI-as-analyst mechanism, primary source.
key_facts: Pipeline: steal (browser creds, cookies, cards, crypto wallets, SSH/cloud keys, Wi-Fi) -> enrich (Gmail receipts, food-delivery history, Roblox inventory lookup) -> build Identity_Report.txt dossier -> send as JSON to OpenRouter -> get AI_Analysis.txt ranking 'WHAT THEY'RE WORTH' and 'THEIR OPSEC' -> exfiltrate both zipped.
Default model anthropic/claude-opus-4.6, fallback chain moonshotai/kimi-k2 then google/gemini-2.5-flash, temperature 0.2; malware detects refusal phrases and advances the chain.
Talos frames this as 'effort displacement': an LLM replaces the operator's manual triage/analysis step, not code generation or evasion.
Reported by Cisco Talos (author Ryan Fetterman) via its CAIRN research effort.

stories.title: Do the math: How we took over ChatGPT accounts
stories.reason: Reproduced, patched ChatGPT web-app exploit chain (MathLive postMessage -> innerHTML injection -> unsandboxed iframe -> YouTube CSP bypass) let a single shared chat link run attacker JS as chatgpt.com and read a victim's private chats; disclosed, fixed, bounty paid.
key_facts: MathLive's postMessage listener accepted messages from any origin and inserted raw HTML via innerHTML; one message could create an unsandboxed iframe inheriting chatgpt.com origin.
ChatGPT's CSP blocked inline scripts but allowed YouTube's oEmbed endpoint, which the chain abused to execute attacker JS on the chatgpt.com origin.
Attacker code could call authenticated ChatGPT APIs: list conversations, open a private chat never shared with the attacker, exfiltrate pieces of it.
Reported to OpenAI bug bounty Oct 18; severity raised P2->P1 Oct 21; fix shipped across two web frontend versions, confirmed fixed Oct 26; $5,000 bounty paid.
Researchers: Parameter (parameter.ai); writeup republished/discussed by Simon Willison and The Hacker News.

stories.title: Chinese Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX to Target Over 200 Organizations Worldwide
stories.reason: Nation-state actor (Vapor Panda/China) ran an AI-orchestrated pentesting framework (ARTEX) with planner/worker LLM agents across 200+ orgs, confirmed by CrowdStrike and Zscaler with concrete technical chain details.
key_facts: ARTEX: Go-based AI pentesting framework by developer 'Autumn-27' (Li Puhua), now closed-source; orchestrates multiple LLM backends (DeepSeek + an unnamed commercial model) via planner/worker agents under human supervision.
CrowdStrike: one intrusion's planning agents consumed ~1.4B input tokens.
Starting Oct 17, 2026: 200+ orgs targeted, post-exploitation confirmed at 9 (BLOODALCHEMY/ShadowPad derivative deployed), credential scanning at 12+ more.
Targets: foreign ministries across 4 continents, 19 US orgs, telecoms in US/Belgium/Philippines.
Chained technique: unsigned SAML assertion + XXE to reach cloud instance metadata, LAPS reads, RBCD, forged admin tokens via keys unrotated since 2022, reused leaked 2024 VPN config/client key.
Sources: CrowdStrike ('Vapor Panda uses ARTEX...'), Zscaler ThreatLabz, WSJ report on the developer.

stories.title: wici-ai/inferssd
stories.reason: Inference-serving infra: llama.cpp-based runtime streams MoE experts from SSD so models too big for RAM/VRAM run, with large vendor-reported throughput gains - squarely on the inference-infra beat.
key_facts: wici-ai/inferssd: streams MoE experts from disk (not KV-cache offload); GGUF files, OpenAI-compatible API + browser UI; supports DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and Muse-Spark-Open.
Vendor-reported 4K-prompt/256-token benchmarks vs llama.cpp: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill 8.06->164.5 tok/s (20.4x) on RTX 5090, decode 0.867->7.27 tok/s (8.4x); on DGX Spark prefill 46.7x.
Not independently verified by the author of the summary.

stories.title: Memdoor: A team of 5 Qwen3.8-27B models beats Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard
stories.reason: Multi-agent decomposition (5x Qwen3.8-27B via Memdoor) matches/beats a larger frontier model on LiveCodeBench Hard with running code and transparent numbers/caveats - concrete eval-methodology result, not just a benchmark claim.
key_facts: Memdoor team-solve: 5 file-communicating roles (planner, 2 ideators, solver, manager) + repair worker, each fresh-context; shell-script test harness decides success, one repair round, no human gate.
5-pass avg on first 10 LiveCodeBench Hard problems: Memdoor 9.8/10 vs authors' own harness 9.6/10 vs Fable 5 alone 8.0/10.
50 runs: 49 solved; total cost $35.79; median run $0.39 / 40 minutes.
Author-noted caveats: only 10 problems, possible training-data contamination, Fable 5 baseline not rerun in this harness, used OpenRouter not authors' own FP8 vLLM setup.

stories.title: bilibili/Index-Translate
stories.reason: Genuine open-weight model family release (2B/9B/35B-A3B checkpoints + quantized builds, Apache-2.0) with published benchmarks - matches the always-surface open-weight criterion.
key_facts: bilibili Index-Translate: multilingual/multimodal translation family on Qwen3.5 - text+image translation, speech dubbing (Index-Echo), syllable-budget translation (Index-Homura), long-document translation (Index-NativeLong); 150 languages.
Published weights: 2B, 9B, 35B-A3B (preview) on HF/ModelScope, plus GGUF/FP8/FP4 quantized builds; Apache-2.0 license.
Self-reported benchmarks: FLORES COMET-22 up to 0.8794 (35B-A3B); WMT26 judge score up to 76.76; beats/trails GPT-5.6-Sol and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on different metrics.

stories.title: microsoft/TokenEconomizer
stories.reason: Open-source coding-agent plugin with a measured SWE-Bench cost/accuracy tradeoff (18-31% cheaper, pass@1 mostly up) across 5 agent/model combos - exactly the concrete-differentiator bar the agent-tooling learned rule requires.
key_facts: microsoft/TokenEconomizer: micro-skills (cached repo facts), tool pruning, and a judge-model failure-loop nudge; doesn't touch model/weights, rides the user's existing agent login.
SWE-Bench, 277 tasks x 6 repos x 5 agent/model combos: mean cost down 18.4-30.9%, cheaper in all 30 cells; pass@1 up in 4/5 combos (down 1.0 pt for Claude Code+Opus 4.8).
Also reports 16-21% lower Web-Bench cost and 6-20% lower on two security-auditing benchmarks (self-reported, unverified independently).
